name: Firecrawl
summary: Firecrawl is a hosted API that turns any web page into clean Markdown or structured data ready for an AI model, handling JavaScript rendering for you.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan gives 1,000 scraping credits a month, refreshed monthly with no credit card required, and a basic page scrape costs 1 credit.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Hobby plan is $19/month billed monthly (or $16/month billed yearly) for 5,000 credits a month and 5 concurrent requests.

portability.note: The API and SDKs are specific to Firecrawl, though the Markdown or HTML it hands back is a standard format, so only the fetching code needs rewriting if you switch providers.

scraper_runs.note: You call the Scrape endpoint with a URL and Firecrawl's own servers fetch and render the page and hand back the content.

js_rendering.note: Every scrape runs in a real browser on Firecrawl's side by default, so a JavaScript-heavy page still costs the same 1 credit as a static page.

ai_ready_output.note: The Scrape endpoint returns the page as clean Markdown (or structured JSON) meant to be fed straight to an AI model.

price_per_1k_pages.value: About $3.80 per 1,000 pages on Hobby ($19/month for 5,000 credits, 1 credit per basic page, JavaScript rendering included at no extra cost). Turning on structured JSON extraction costs 5 credits a page instead of 1, about $19 per 1,000 pages.
price_per_1k_pages.note: Math from the Hobby plan price and credit allowance; 1 credit covers one rendered page, and JSON-format extraction adds 4 more credits per page.

setup.step: Create a free Firecrawl account and copy your API key from the dashboard at firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys.
Install the SDK with npm install firecrawl.
Add your key as FIRECRAWL_API_KEY in your environment file.
In a server route (for example app/api/scrape/route.ts), create a Firecrawl client and call firecrawl.scrape(url, { formats: ['markdown'] }) to get the page back as Markdown.

builder_notes: Keep FIRECRAWL_API_KEY server-side and call the SDK from a route handler or server action, never from client code.
Store the Markdown you get back instead of re-scraping the same URL, since every scrape spends a credit.
Check the target site's robots.txt and terms before scraping it; Firecrawl fetches the page but does not decide whether you're allowed to use it.
